messages.content: my teacher sent me a question at night. does that mean i have to answer at night?
not from the time of the message alone. you would need to know whether the teacher asked for an answer now or gave a time for it.
the message says answer when you have time before tomorrow afternoon.
then you can answer before tomorrow afternoon. it does not ask you to answer during the night.
can i write a short message saying i saw it and will answer in the morning?
yes. you can say: i have seen your question. i will answer in the morning.
what if i am not sure i will have time in the morning?
then do not give morning as a sure plan. you can say you have seen the question and will answer before tomorrow afternoon, if you know you can do that.
write that message.
i have seen your question and will answer before tomorrow afternoon.
why does seeing a message not mean i am ready to answer it?
you may need time to think, find information, or finish another task. knowing the question and knowing the answer are different things.
make that explanation shorter.
you can read a question before you have the answer ready.
only give the message again.
i have seen your question and will answer before tomorrow afternoon.
can long be used about a road and a conversation?
yes. a long road goes far from one end to the other. a long conversation takes a long time. the same word can be useful for different things in context.
what does long give us about the road?
it gives an idea of how far the road goes from one end to the other, rather than how long people spend talking.
can a short road take a long time to walk?
yes. you might walk slowly, stop to talk, or wait along the way. how far the road goes is not the only thing that changes the time.
give that explanation more simply.
how far the road goes is not the only thing that changes how long the walk takes.
now give one sentence with a short road and a long walk.
the road was short, but we stopped to talk, so the walk took a long time.
what does longer mean in the road is longer than the street?
it is about how far the two go, rather than how much time you spend walking on them.
so does it tell me the time i will take?
no. you might walk fast or slowly, and you might stop. the sentence gives the size of the road and street, not your walking time.
can you know which one i should take without more information?
no. i would need to know where you want to go, how much time you have, and what each way is like.
write a story about a person saying i am ready while other people are still getting ready. keep it about going to the park.

a child stood by the door with his things and said he was ready to go to the park. his sister was still looking for her book, and his father was putting water into a container. the child asked why they were not leaving if he was ready. his father explained that one person being ready did not mean the whole group was ready. the child sat down near the door and asked whether there was something he could help with. his sister asked him to look on the desk for her book. he found it there. soon they were all at the door, and this time they could leave together.
what did i am ready tell the family?
it told them that the child was ready. it did not say whether anyone else was ready.
why was helping with the book useful?
his sister needed the book before leaving, and he had time to help look for it.
was waiting the same as doing nothing useful?
not in this story. while he waited, he helped with something the group still needed.
write his question to the family.
i am ready. is there anything i can help with while we wait?
can that question tell us what help is needed?
not by itself. it asks the other people to say what they need.
finish with the group leaving, without another explanation at the end.
his father closed the container, his sister held her book, and they walked through the door together.
my friend said we could visit the market this week. is that already a plan?
it sounds like an idea, but not a full plan yet. you have not given a day, time, or whether you both chose to go.
i want to say the idea sounds good without saying yes to any day.
you could say: that sounds like a good idea. which day were you thinking about?
what if i do not know which days i am free yet?
then you can say that too. you can like the idea without knowing when you can do it.
write both parts in a short reply.
that sounds like a good idea. i need to check when i am free before we choose a day.
can you leave the choice open for them too?
that sounds like a good idea. we can both check when we are free, then choose a day if it works.
does if it works mean i do not want to go?
not by itself. it leaves room for the time or other details to make the visit possible or not. you can like the idea and still need to check.
make that explanation shorter.
not by itself. you can like the idea and still need a time that works for both of you.
only give the short message again.
that sounds like a good idea. we can both check when we are free, then choose a day if it works.
i wrote three stories in my book. i wrote one of those stories again on a page for my friend. how many different stories did i write?
three different stories. writing one again on another page does not make it a different story by itself.
how many pages have stories on them if each story in my book takes one page?
four pages have stories on them: three in your book and one for your friend.
how many different original stories are on those four pages?
three different original stories are on them. the page for your friend has one of those stories again.
explain how my book and the other page are different.
your book has three stories. the other page has just one of those three.
if my friend gives the page back, does my book get a new story?
no. the page has a story already in the book. returning the page does not add a different story to the book.
what if i change the last part of the story on the page for my friend?
then the page has a changed story. the first part may stay the same, but the last part is different from the story in your book.
say that more simply.
then the page is not the same as before. it has your story with a new last part.
only give the number of different original stories again.
three.
i walked around the park and came home without doing anything else. i liked it, but it feels like i should have done more.
you can enjoy a walk without turning it into another task. what did you like while you were there?
i liked seeing the trees and not looking at my phone.
those were real parts of the time you had. you said you liked the walk, even without doing another task.
can you say that without telling me how to feel?
you said you liked the trees and the time away from your phone. those are the reasons you gave for why you liked the walk.
write a sentence i can use about the day.
i went to the park, looked at the trees, and enjoyed not looking at my phone for a while.
what if someone asks what i got done?
you can say you went for a walk. you do not need to make up another task to make the answer sound larger.
can you make that answer kind and simple?
i just went for a walk and enjoyed some time in the park.
only give the sentence about the trees again.
i went to the park, looked at the trees, and enjoyed not looking at my phone for a while.
write a story about a child saying he found an object and then learning to give useful details. do not use a more specific name for the object.

a child came into the room and told his mother that he had found an object outside. she asked what it was like. he said it was small, made a sound when moved, and had been on the road near their door. she told him not to choose what it was for just from those details. he put it where she could see it without using it. they talked about what they knew: its size, where he found it, and what happened when it moved. they still did not know who had left it or what its use was. the general word object let him start the story, and the details helped his mother understand what he had seen.
what did the word object not tell her?
it did not tell her its specific name, use, or whose it was.
why did the details help?
they gave information she could use even though he did not know its name.
can you know the object was a toy?
no. a small object that makes a sound could be many things. the story does not give enough to call it a toy.
what question could she ask about the place?
where on the road did you find it?
answer without making up a more specific place.
i found it on the road near our door.
finish with one question still open.
they could say where it had been found, but still did not know who had left it there.
what is the difference between then and than?
then can put things in order: i ate, then i read. than can give the difference between things: this book is longer than that one.
use both in one small story.
i chose the shorter book. then i found it had more hard words than the longer one.
now make it about how easy the reading was, rather than the words.
i chose the shorter book. then i found it was not as easy to read as the longer one.
is a shorter book always easy to read?
no. fewer pages can still have hard words or ideas. the number of pages does not tell us everything about the reading.
give that explanation in one sentence.
a short book can still have hard words and ideas.
now only give a sentence with then about making tea.
i washed the cup, then made tea.
now only than about two cups.
this cup is larger than that one.
why not this cup is larger then that one?
use than when saying how the size of one cup is different from the other. then is for order or time in the examples we used.
